About the company

Trust Wallet is the secure, self-custody Web3 wallet that empowers people to own and control their digital assets. Whether you're new to crypto or an experienced user, Trust Wallet makes it easier, safer, and more convenient to explore Web3, securely access dApps, manage your crypto, and buy and sell digital assets, all in one place.

About the program:

The Trust Wallet Management Trainee Program is a selective, fast-track start to a career in Product, Marketing or Business Development in Web3. You’ll join a small cohort and work on live products used by millions of people from day one. You’ll work directly with senior leaders across product, engineering, marketing, BD and the wider business.

We’re looking for early-career talent who question assumptions and bring fresh perspectives to self-custody, payments and the agentic AI economy.

What you’ll do

  • Own real, scoped work with clear outcomes and ship it.

  • Research the market and competitors: wallets, DEXs, DeFi trading platforms, stablecoins and payment networks.

  • Explore what’s next in agentic payments, where AI agents transact on-chain for users.

  • Use data to decide: set KPIs, run experiments and measure impact.

  • Pitch your ideas to leadership. The best ones get built, launched or signed.

Track-specific work

  • Product: Turn user problems into PRDs, user stories and success metrics. Work with engineering, design and data to ship features.

  • Marketing: Shape positioning and go-to-market for new features. Run campaigns across X, community and content, and own growth experiments end to end.

  • Business Development: Map and qualify partners across chains, dApps, stablecoin issuers and payment providers. Support deal pitches and integrations from first conversation to launch.

What we’re looking for

  • 0–2 years of work experience, including internships. A degree in any field is welcome, as long as you can show strong analytical thinking.

  • Structured and logical: you can break a messy problem into clear parts and a recommendation.

  • Clear communicator, in writing and in person. You can explain a complex idea simply.

  • AI-native: you use AI tools (e.g. Claude, Grok, Cursor) in your daily work and are curious about AI agents.

  • Genuinely interested in Web3: you’ve used a wallet, a DEX or stablecoins, and you can talk about what works and what’s broken.

  • A fast learner with strong ownership, comfortable with ambiguity and pace

Nice-to-have

  • Hands-on Web3 experience: DeFi, perpetuals trading, stablecoin payments, hackathons or DAO contributions.

  • Side projects, a product teardown, a newsletter, or an active X/GitHub presence.

What you’ll get

  • A structured program with mentorship from senior leaders across different functional teams.

  • Real ownership of features used by millions of people.

  • Front-row exposure to AI × crypto payments

Additional Information

This is a global and fully remote role. You must have the right to work for the country you are based.

Why work at Trust Wallet?

  • Be a part of the world’s leading blockchain ecosystem that continues to grow.

  • Excellent learning and career development opportunities.

  • Work alongside diverse, world-class talent, in an environment where learning and growth opportunities are endless.

  • Tackle fast-paced, challenging and unique projects.

  • Work in a truly global organization, with international teams and a flat organizational structure.

  • Work fully remotely with flexible working hours.

  • Enjoy competitive salary and benefits.

Apply today to join our team in building the world’s most trusted and secure crypto wallet and enable a decentralized future for everyone.

Trust Wallet is committed to being an equal opportunity employer. We believe that having a diverse workforce is fundamental to our success.

This is a sales-focused role for someone who knows how to turn existing customer relationships into meaningful revenue opportunities. You’ll own a portfolio of accounts, develop and execute account growth plans, identify new use cases, expand product adoption, negotiate commercial agreements, and build a strong pipeline of expansion opportunities.

You’ll work closely with Customer Success Managers to help clients unlock more value from BVNK while driving measurable commercial results. You’ll be accountable for growing revenue within your portfolio, protecting and expanding existing business, and identifying opportunities to deepen BVNK’s role in our customers’ payment infrastructure.

We’re looking for a proactive, entrepreneurial account manager who combines strong relationship-building skills with a sales hunter’s mindset. You should be comfortable owning commercial conversations, challenging the status quo, and consistently finding ways to grow your accounts.

Key Areas of Responsibilities:

  • Own account growth and revenue: Develop and execute strategic account plans to drive revenue expansion, increase share of wallet, and grow the value of your portfolio.
  • Build and manage an expansion pipeline: Proactively identify, qualify, and progress upsell, cross-sell, new use case, and new market opportunities within existing accounts.

  • Own the customer relationship: Build trusted relationships with key decision-makers, including executive stakeholders, commercial leaders, and operational teams. Establish BVNK as a strategic partner in their growth.

  • A sales-first mindset: You’re proactive, commercially curious, and motivated by winning business. You don’t wait for opportunities to come to you; you find them, build a case, and close them.

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Getting paid is still one of the most manual parts of running a business. Finance teams chase invoices over email, match payments to invoices by hand in spreadsheets, and close the books late because cash data is scattered across banks, payment processors, and ERPs.

Ramp's Accounts Receivable team is building the system that automates all of it, from the moment an invoice is sent to the moment cash is reconciled in the general ledger. We own the full receivables lifecycle: invoicing, collections, payments, cash application, and accounting sync.

We're looking for a senior backend engineer to own core pieces of that system. The work sits where hard engineering problems meet real money: matching messy payment data to the right invoices, keeping ledgers correct to the cent, and syncing reliably with the accounting systems our customers depend on. You'll own projects end to end, from design through production, and work closely with product and design to turn complex finance workflows into software that just works.


What You’ll Do

  • Build the payment-matching systems that automatically apply incoming ACH, wire, card, and check payments to the right invoices, even when payment details are incomplete or inconsistent

  • Design accurate data models where every dollar is traceable from invoice to payment to general ledger

  • Build two-way integrations with ERPs like NetSuite and QuickBooks that stay consistent through retries, partial failures, and edits on either side

  • Build collections workflows that help businesses get paid faster without hurting their customer relationships

  • Own projects from problem definition and technical design through launch, monitoring, and iteration

  • Raise the engineering bar through design reviews, code reviews, and mentorship

What You’ll Need

  • Product sense: you care about the customer problem, not just the ticket, and you push back when the spec is wrong

  • Experience designing and operating production backend systems, including APIs, data models, and asynchronous workflows

  • Strong system design judgment and the ability to balance speed, correctness, reliability, and simplicity

  • A track record of independently owning complex projects and shipping high-quality software

  • Strong communication skills and a collaborative approach to technical decisions

Nice to Haves

  • Experience with invoicing, billing, payments, accounting, or other financial workflows

  • Experience building integrations that keep data consistent across systems

  • Experience improving reliability and operational visibility in a growing product

Elliptic is the leader in digital asset decisioning, we have built the most comprehensive platform for efficiently extracting crypto data and intelligence across blockchains with the greatest accuracy.

Our platform’s unrivalled uptime, scalability, depth and breadth of our data and intelligence means exacting organizations choose Elliptic for their compliance, risk management, intelligence operations and blockchain infrastructure needs.

Founded in 2013, Elliptic is headquartered in London with offices in New York, Washington D.C., UAE, Singapore and Tokyo. To learn more, visit www.elliptic.co and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

 

Do you want to lead a data science team on a problem the industry has not solved yet, while still writing code yourself? Are you excited about building the data foundation for how compliance works when the customer is an autonomous agent rather than a person? Are you looking for a values led company where a small team is trusted with a question that matters commercially in months, not years?

 

The impact you will have:

You will lead data science inside Elliptic's Intelligence team, alongside Intelligence Collection, Research and Investigations, and Professional Services. This is deliberately a player-coach role with a prospect of scaling a team. At first you will lead a small team of data scientists and you are expected to own the team's direction, performance and growth. You will own the evidence for the models your team builds, and you will represent them at Elliptic's model risk governance forum. This is not a compliance tax bolted onto the technical work: it is the reason institutions trust our outputs.

The reason we are hiring a lead as we add more data scientists is that a small team working on an unsolved problem needs someone who intrinsically understands the domain, not a layer of management above it. You will set what this team works on, hire the next people into it, and be the person whose technical judgement the team trusts because you can do the work yourself.

 

What you will do:

  • Lead and grow the team. Set objectives with your data scientists in the context of company strategy, own their performance and development, and be the manager who has the difficult conversation rather than deferring it. Level the team against Elliptic's Intelligence career framework and build real development paths.

  • Hire the next data scientists. Own the hiring process end to end with support: levels, job descriptions, hiring plan, interview panel and bar, and the hiring decision. Team growth to seven to nine people over time depends on you getting this right early.

  • Build the collection for the future of compliance. Take it from a directive to a specification to delivered data: define what good looks like, sequence the work, set the quality bar, and be honest about what the dataset does and does not support.

  • Own model governance for your team's models. Keep the model inventory current and correctly tiered, make sure validation and testing evidence exists at the standard each tier requires, monitor for drift and act on threshold breaches, and submit material changes and production deployments for review with the testing artefacts attached. Own the remediation of issues raised against your models, to agreed deadlines.

  • Lead Elliptic's data science work. Frame the research question, run the first experiments, and form a defensible view of what Elliptic needs to be able to do and by when. Bring that view to Intelligence leadership, the Chief Scientist and Product as a recommendation rather than as an open question.

  • Stay technically hands on. Write code, review your team's work at the level of method rather than output, and make the method calls yourself when they matter.

  • Own the team's existing commitments. The team's current work on clustering, attribution, heuristics and labelling continues to serve the platform. You own its reliability and its trade offs, and you decide what to stop.

  • Work across functions. Partner with Intelligence Collection, Collection Engineering, Research and Investigations, the Chief Scientist, Product and Engineering, so that data science work lands as platform capability rather than as analysis nobody uses.

  • Set the AI working standard for the team. Decide how your team uses AI in its engineering and research workflow, what must be verified and how, and hold the team to it.

 

What you will achieve in the first 6 months:

  • The collection plan delivered at a scale that supports real model or heuristic work, with a documented path to maintaining it.

  • An agreed Elliptic position on the evolution of compliance systems, timed against expected industry demand, with the first capability work either underway or deliberately deferred with stated reasons.

  • At least one data science hire made, and the existing levelled against the career framework with development plans in place.

  • Model governance in good standing for everything your team owns: inventory current and correctly tiered, no overdue validations on the highest tiers, monitoring in place with acted-upon thresholds, and no open issues past their remediation deadline.

  • Data science objectives for Intelligence agreed and delivering, with other functions able to state what they can expect from the team and when.

  • A visible improvement in the reliability or throughput of the team's core output, attributable to a change you made.

  • Technical credibility intact: the team takes your method judgements seriously because you can do the work.

 

You will be a great fit here if you:

  • Want to lead a team without leaving the technical work behind, and can say honestly where you draw that line.

  • Are comfortable being accountable for a question nobody has answered yet, including for saying what you do not know.

  • Treat management as the work rather than as overhead: objectives, feedback, development and difficult conversations included.

  • Treat governance as part of building good models rather than as paperwork that follows them, and would rather surface a problem with your own model than have someone else find it.

  • Are pragmatic about trade offs between rigour and speed, and can explain the trade off you chose.

  • Make other teams more effective rather than treating them as consumers of your team's output.

  • Are curious about how the company operates beyond your own function.

  • Care about the mission of using intelligence to fight financial crime and protect the global financial system.

 

Our ideal candidate has:

  • AI fluency, which is essential for this role. You must be able to demonstrate how you apply AI tools and approaches within a data science workflow: writing and debugging code, exploring unfamiliar data, accelerating pipeline and model work, and automating repetitive tasks. You must also be able to show how you critically evaluate the output, where you would not rely on it, and how you set verification expectations for a team rather than only for yourself. This is assessed in a dedicated stage of the interview process, working with your own tooling.

  • Demonstrated experience managing data scientists or machine learning engineers: setting objectives, owning performance including underperformance, and developing people. You can point to someone whose career changed because of how you managed them.

  • Experience hiring into a technical team, including defining the bar rather than only sitting on panels.

  • Deep, hands on data science and machine learning capability that is current. Strong Python and SQL, and the ability to interrogate large behavioural or transactional datasets yourself and defend your method under challenge.

  • A track record of taking an ambiguous question to a delivered dataset, model or capability, including deciding what was good enough.

  • Experience with a modern data stack comparable to ours: a cloud data lake, Spark or Databricks, and AWS.

  • Clear communication with technical and non technical stakeholders, and the ability to cascade direction to a team so that each person knows why their work matters.

 

Bonus Points for:

  • Work on agentic systems, LLM agents or autonomous transaction flows, whether in compliance, payments, fraud or infrastructure.

  • Experience building a large dataset or collection from nothing, including the unglamorous parts: schema decisions, quality checks, and maintenance.

  • Blockchain or on chain data experience: clustering, attribution, heuristics, anomaly detection, mempool analysis, or research into privacy preserving systems.

  • Experience in payments, fraud or risk data science, where the cost of a false negative is commercial rather than academic.

  • Having grown a team from a few people to a full department, and being able to describe what broke on the way.

  • A PhD or equivalent research training, or a record of published applied research.

  • Experience in a regulated environment or with model risk management frameworks, whether in financial services, or as a vendor to it, or in another domain with equivalent assurance requirements.

  • Cycle to Work Scheme

What is Kalshi?

Kalshi has defined a new category: prediction markets. Kalshi allows people to trade on the outcome of any events and turn any question about the future into a financial asset. Kalshi fought for years and legalized prediction markets in the US for the first time in history, is currently the fastest growing financial market in America, and has thousands of markets across politics, economics, financials, weather, tech, AI, culture and more.

We believe prediction markets have the potential to be the largest financial market because they turn anything into a financial position.

  • Our vision: well… build the largest financial market on the planet.

  • Our mission: bring more truth to the world through the power of markets.

Our culture is simple: we hire really talented people, work really hard, and enjoy the climb. We are looking for ambitious and exceptional people to join our (relatively small) team to help us build the next generation of financial markets.

Role Roadmap

In the Sports Operations function at Kalshi, you'll be a critical member ensuring our sports markets run flawlessly. The Sports Operations team is responsible for the precise execution of sports market listings, determinations, and maintaining the integrity of our sports prediction markets.

What You'll Do

  • Execute the listing of sports markets with precision, ensuring all markets are properly configured and accurately reflect game conditions, player availability, and league rules. Make rapid determinations on market outcomes based on official league data, box scores, and verified sports sources while managing time-sensitive settlement windows.

  • Structure sports markets to capture the true axis of disagreement between traders, understanding the nuances between different contract types (spreads, totals, props, futures). Make strategic decisions about how to frame markets around games, seasons, player performances, and sporting events to maximize liquidity and trading interest.

  • Build out and prioritize the sports market listing pipeline across all major leagues (NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, MLS, NCAA) and international competitions. Balance pre-game, in-play, and futures markets while responding to breaking news like injuries, trades, and lineup changes that affect market demand and trading volumes.

  • Leverage deep understanding of how sportsbooks operate to identify market opportunities, understand edge cases in settlement scenarios, and ensure our markets capture the sophistication that sports traders expect. Navigate complex scenarios like postponements, player scratches, overtime rules, and stat corrections.

  • Maintain encyclopedic knowledge of league-specific rules, tiebreakers, playoff structures, and statistical definitions across all sports. Ensure markets are structured with airtight settlement criteria that account for sport-specific edge cases (rain delays, technical fouls, injury timeouts, VAR decisions, etc.).

  • Monitor live games and sports news across multiple leagues simultaneously, quickly responding to events that require market suspension, clarification, or settlement. Manage high-volume periods like NFL Sundays or March Madness with precision while multitasking across numerous concurrent events.

  • Work with structured, time-sensitive sports data feeds to ensure accurate market parameters, real-time updates, and proper settlement. Identify and resolve data discrepancies quickly to maintain market integrity.

  • Issue timely clarifications on sports markets when ambiguities arise (injury designations, weather impacts, rule interpretations), maintaining trader trust through clear, authoritative communications about sports-specific situations.

  • Work closely with Contracts, Product, and Engineering teams to implement sports-specific operational improvements, integrate new data sources, and expand our sports market offerings.

What You Bring

  • Bachelor's degree in finance, economics, business, sports management, mathematics, or a related field.

  • Encyclopedic knowledge of sports across multiple leagues with deep understanding of rules, playoff structures, tiebreakers, and statistical categories for NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, MLS, and major NCAA sports.

  • Extensive experience with sportsbooks – understanding how sportsbooks operate, common market types, settlement procedures, and the edge cases that arise in sports market operations.

  • Experience working with structured, time-sensitive sports data including real-time feeds, official league data sources, and sports statistics platforms.

  • Genuine passion for sports with the ability to follow multiple games simultaneously and stay current on player news, injuries, trades, and team dynamics across all major leagues.

  • Exceptional multitasking abilities to manage numerous live markets during peak periods while maintaining accuracy in high-pressure, time-sensitive situations.

  • Deep understanding of sportsbook nuances and edge cases including suspended games, protest outcomes, stat corrections, and unusual scoring scenarios that affect market settlement.

  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to quickly interpret box scores, game situations, and official rulings to make sound operational decisions.

  • Experience trading on Kalshi, sportsbooks, DFS platforms, or other prediction markets is strongly preferred.

  • Excellent written communication skills for drafting clear market clarifications on complex sports scenarios and settlement decisions.

  • Ability to work flexible hours including nights and weekends to cover live sporting events across different time zones.

  • Hardworking mentality with a commitment to operational excellence and the stamina to maintain focus during extended periods of live sports coverage.

NYC Pay Transparency Disclosure

Salary Range: $120,000 to $180,000 annually plus equity and benefits. This salary range is based on the current available market data, and represents the expected salary range for this role. Kalshi has minimal hierarchy and few titles, but has broad ranges of experience represented within roles. Should you have compensation expectations that exceed these bands, we'd love to hear from you and would welcome you to reach out to further discuss.

Our Culture

Meritocracy is at our core, and we value people who take ownership and figure (usually hard) things out. We dream big. We love our craft deeply and are proud of what we put out in the world. We are committed to our vision of building something big… but also useful: a product that brings more truth through the power of markets.

Kalshians are Kalshi’s most important asset: we pick Kalshians carefully, so we trust them fully on day 1.

Kalshi is committed to creating a culture of inclusion and belonging, and we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We believe it is our collective responsibility to uphold these values and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to join us in our mission. All qualified applicants will be treated with respect and receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, uniform service, veteran status, age, or any other protected characteristic per federal, state, or local law. If you are passionate about what you do and want to use your talents to support our mission and values, we’d love to hear from you.

Working closely with external protocol teams and Mysten’s own DeFi products, including DeepBook, you’ll help address risks before they become incidents and strengthen security across the ecosystem

About Open Standard

Open Standard is building internet-native money. Data moved to the cloud, and dollars will move onchain. When they do, stablecoins become core financial infrastructure.

Our stablecoin, Open USD (OUSD), is built for that shift. Minting and redeeming are free at any volume. Nearly all reserve revenue goes back to the businesses that grow adoption. The partners who use OUSD govern it, rather than a single issuer.

OUSD is live on Base, Ethereum, Solana, and Tempo. Our founding partners are Coinbase, Mastercard, Shopify, Stripe, and Visa, and more than 200 banks, payment networks, fintechs, and crypto companies have signed up to use OUSD. Our CEO is Zach Abrams, who co-founded Bridge (acquired by Stripe for $1.1B) and previously led product at Brex, Coinbase, and Square.

OS is currently a team of about ten. We have a real shot at being the next inevitable transformation in stablecoins. We're hiring someone to help make us inevitable.

The role

We're hiring a Deputy General Counsel to help build the legal function at Open Standard alongside our General Counsel, a Founding Team member of Open Standard, who was also part of the founding team of Bridge. You'll be a partner to the GC, not a direct report in the usual sense. The two of you will divide the work by comparative advantage, and you'll own your areas end to end. We are AI-centric, highly scaled, and don't plan on building a large legal team for the foreseeable future. You'll do the work yourself, with AI agents and a tight group of outside counsel extending your reach.

Legal sits at the center of OS's business. You'll be integrated into OUSD design choices, partner deals, and launch decisions, all of which present needle moving commercial opportunities that depend on thoughtful legal decision making that unlocks value for the business.

What you'll do

  • Shape the product with our product and engineering teams: mint and redemption flows, partner rewards, wallet and chain integrations, and new use cases from cross-border payments to agentic commerce.

  • Structure and negotiate the deals OUSD runs on: network partner agreements, reserve and custody relationships, exchange and liquidity arrangements, and agreements with chains and protocols.

  • Work directly with the world's largest banks, card networks, and asset managers, answering their diligence, risk, and regulatory questions with credibility.

  • Find the creative structure when the easy answer is "no": the deal term, product change, or regulatory path that gets a partner live.

  • Help steward a new kind of governance model, with a company owned and governed by the partners who use its product.

  • Support our Head of Policy on regulator and policymaker engagement, comment letters, and industry work.

  • Assist with regulatory strategy for OUSD under the GENIUS Act and state and international regimes. This covers licensing paths, issuer and reserve arrangements, and how rewards and distribution are treated.

  • Build an AI-native legal function, using agents and workflows for contract review, diligence questionnaires, regulatory tracking, and partner questions.

  • Manage outside counsel in the US and abroad tightly, and know when not to use them.

You may be a good fit if you

  • Have 10+ years of legal experience, including substantial in-house time at crypto companies.

  • Know the stablecoin market cold from three angles: commercial, regulatory, and product. You can explain how issuers make money, how reserves and redemption work, what GENIUS changes, and where the market is going next.

  • Have worked with or inside large financial institutions and understand how banks, card networks, and asset managers make decisions. You earn their trust without starting to act like them.

  • Have creative commercial instincts and use them to shape deals and products, not just paper them. You're a regulatory and product lawyer who structures deals, not a contracts specialist who knows crypto.

  • Are scrappy and do the work yourself, from the first draft to the board memo.

  • Already use AI seriously in your practice, and have built agents or workflows that expand what one lawyer can do.

  • Write clearly and precisely, because most decisions here start in writing.

  • Are admitted to practice in a US jurisdiction.

Strong candidates may also have

  • Worked in-house at a stablecoin issuer

  • Worked in a bank's digital assets group, alongside crypto-native experience

  • Worked on stablecoin or payments licensing: trust charters, state money transmission, or non-US regimes such as MiCA

  • Helped build the legal function at an early-stage company

  • Relationships with regulators, policymakers, or industry groups in payments and digital assets
